currentContext.strengths: Category leadership in incense: 'We are already the number one player and continue to gain market share rapidly', and the category is described as accretive to both revenue and profit growth - against a GCPL average net contribution of around 100 rupees, incense delivers roughly 80-85|Long-cycle R&D depth: upcoming launches in hair and household insecticides in areas where the company says it has 'invested nearly a decade in research and development', with an innovation pipeline 'stronger than it has ever been'|Distribution and mass-market execution: management self-assesses GCPL at the '80th or 90th percentile' on the classic FMCG playbook of big SKUs, general trade distribution and television-led media (and candidly at the ~50th percentile on e-commerce, digital marketing and AI)|Structural health of the base business: penetration and market share in key categories have trended well, and India standalone non-soaps volume growth moved from low single digits in FY2022 to the teens in FY2026|Sustainability standing: ranked number 1 on the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Sustainability Indices in FMCG this year|Brand and group heritage: part of the Godrej Industries Group, crafting products since 1897, with 15% of the group owned by an independent philanthropic trust
currentContext.strategies: Aligning climate disclosure more closely with the TCFD framework in the current reporting cycle - covering climate governance, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, scenario analysis, metrics and targets - and preparing a first standalone TCFD report, alongside continued reporting through Integrated Annual Reports, CDP and DJSI|Board-level climate oversight: a dedicated Board-level Sustainability Committee led by the Chair of the Board oversees sustainability performance, with the Managing Director and CEO approving climate strategies and reviewing sustainability KPIs quarterly, plus an annual mid-year review of Operating Plans across all organisational levels|De-risking deforestation-linked inputs: sourcing rubber only from India, where it is an agricultural commodity from privately owned agro-forestry plantations with complete traceability|Replacing virgin paper with FSC-certified recycled paper across soap stiffeners, soap wrappers, corrugated boxes, printed cartons, leaflets, stickers, labels and other paper-based packaging, as paper-based packaging is increased to reduce reliance on plastic|Securing high-quality PFAD from multiple regions and geographies to reduce dependency on major palm oil markets, and working with suppliers to raise PFAD environmental standards|Continuing investment in cybersecurity technology, policy compliance and employee awareness - vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, breach simulations and red teaming, with an ISO 27001:2022 certified system and a GRC tool|Compliance monitoring through the internal Legatrix system, giving all manufacturing units and management a one-stop view of statutory compliance, supported by Corporate Affairs, Legal and Audit teams tracking emerging regulation|Talent management and succession planning: annual identification of critical positions and succession coverage, review of talent supply and leadership development initiatives to build succession for key roles|Plastic packaging intensity (weight of packaging to overall product weight) reduced by over 20% from the base year 2019-20, with continued focus on reducing it to cut material consumption, packaging cost and EPR cost across key markets|63% of energy usage in India operations is from renewable sources, following ramped-up renewables investment including a co-generation plant at the flagship Malanpur manufacturing site, briquette-based boilers and microturbines for steam, solar PV and green tariffs where available|Life Cycle Assessments completed for products constituting 56% of revenue, used to identify sustainability improvement areas and to offer products at a 'green discount rather than a green premium' by passing savings to consumers|49% of suppliers by procurement spend evaluated for ESG performance in FY25-26 under GCPL's Policy for Responsible Supply, with industry best practices and suggestive actions shared with suppliers|Consistent record of zero fatalities across offices and manufacturing plants, supported by a Health & Safety policy, a Central Safety Committee and plant-level committees reviewing monthly OHS data|Greener product development, e.g. Godrej Magic Hand Wash, which uses lower water content than alternatives and has lower plastic packaging impact|ESG oversight through a Board-level ESG Committee, a Risk Management Committee-owned ERM framework and a Risk Management Policy, with double-materiality insights integrated into ERM in priority areas (OHS, governance, renewable energy, sustainable supply chain, sustainable packaging)|Double materiality assessment conducted per EFRAG guidance (Feb 2024) and draft ESRS 1, aligned with CSRD, covering operations in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Argentina, Chile, Africa, Indonesia and the USA; 40 topics screened, 47 one-on-one interviews and 184 survey responses narrowed to a top-20 material topic set|Grievance redressal disclosed under BRSR: 136 shareholder complaints filed in FY2025-26 with 2 pending at year end, and 8 employee/worker complaints (POSH) with 2 pending; nil complaints from communities, customers and value chain partners
currentContext.expansion: The report describes manufacturing footprint build-out rather than a rupee capex plan. Project Vindhya, GCPL's second greenfield project in India, was commissioned in March 2024 and is described as delivered in record time and designed to be digitally enabled, sustainably designed and inclusive by intent. A greenfield plant in Tamil Nadu is referenced, and the Chengalpattu manufacturing facility is described as a 27-acre plant built in just 13 months that has created over 1,000 job opportunities with 50% women on the shop floor. Other named sites appearing in the year's awards and operations commentary include the Kathua plant and the Nilgiri plant. On capability expansion: manufacturing enablement for LATAM markets was strengthened through completion of pending ammonia and no-ammonia hair-colour shades, while India continued to serve as a production hub for select international businesses; the hair colour category also progressed through miniaturisation initiatives, expansion of professional shade offerings and development of consumer-centric wet hair products. Nigeria's NAFDAC completed a GMP audit of the Aer pocket line successfully and export production started. R&D-led expansion included entry into new segments (antiperspirants with Bloq, plug-in electric fragrance with Aer Plug Electrical, women's fragrance EDP gift sets under Park Avenue/Kamasutra), a natural-ingredient Rat Repellent Spray, a Dimefluthrin-based Goodknight Aerosol and Liquid Vaporizer relaunch in Nigeria, higher-active Mat and Liquid Vaporizer formats in Indonesia, Renew Shampoo Hair Colour and Inecto Pop Shades and Bleach in South Africa, Hair Super Food variants in Nigeria, and multiple patents filed during the year. A value engineering initiative on the Good Knight device was commercialised, and a green solvent replaced a petroleum-derived solvent in Aerosol.

risks.note: BRSR material issue 1 (Risk, negative implications): physical risk to the workforce in manufacturing operations and frontline distribution teams; inadequate OHS training could cause incidents, accidents and even fatalities, with indirect risk of workplace closures, higher legal and compliance costs, stakeholder scrutiny, lower morale and brand damage. Mitigated by a Health & Safety policy, SOPs, incident investigation, periodic review and a Central Safety Committee plus plant-level committees reviewing monthly data; GCPL cites a consistent record of zero fatalities across offices and plants.

risks.risk: Product safety and quality / evolving ingredient regulation
risks.note: BRSR material issue 2 (Risk, negative implications): an evolving regulatory landscape and changing guidelines on the composition of ingredients and raw materials pose a risk of disruption to operations. Mitigated through quality testing SOPs for all products, raw-material testing procedures and skill-development training.

risks.risk: Business ethics and ethical marketing (greenwashing / labelling)
risks.note: BRSR material issue 3 (Risk, negative implications): greenwashing or ethically and factually incorrect marketing practices and claims pose reputational risk. Mitigated by the code of conduct, whistle blower, anti-sexual harassment, human rights and health & safety policies, and a Responsible Marketing, Advertising and Sales Policy aligned to local and international standards.

BRSR material issue 4 (Risk, negative implications): the need to meet all reporting and transparency requirements of market regulators and to voluntarily disclose against international ESG frameworks. GCPL reports under BRSR in India plus CDP, GRI and Integrated Reporting <IR>.

BRSR material issue 6 (Risk, negative implications): procurement from diverse suppliers carries ESG compliance risk for critical suppliers and unethical sourcing practices. Under the Policy for Responsible Supply, 49% of suppliers by procurement spend were evaluated for ESG performance in FY25-26.

risks.risk: Regulatory pressure on plastic packaging and Extended Producer Responsibility
risks.note: BRSR material issue 5, flagged as an Opportunity: stricter regulation on plastic use, waste generation, disposal and EPR across geographies such as India and Africa is accelerating the transition to sustainable packaging; most GCPL products involve plastic packaging, so plastic packaging intensity and EPR cost are a structural exposure being managed rather than an unaddressed risk.

one-line thesis: GCPL delivered strong Q4FY26 with 11% revenue growth driven by Home Care and International markets, though FY27 margins face near-term pressure from crude oil inflation (7-9%) offset by pricing actions. A significant accounting change netting trade spend against revenue optically boosts margins without altering underlying economics, while the strategic pivot toward high-growth Home Care and Fab portfolio (now ~INR 500cr ARR) signals a structural shift in the growth engine away from muted Personal Care.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +11% YoY (6% volume); EBITDA: +10% YoY, Margin 21.7% (optically higher due to accounting change); PAT: +10% YoY; Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Not explicitly detailed but liquidity unchanged by accounting shift. One-offs: Latin America EBITDA impacted by one-time costs; Accounting distortion: Trade spend reclassified from OpEx to Revenue deduction, inflating margin % but leaving absolute EBITDA/PAT unchanged.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Mid-single-digit volume in Indonesia, double-digit in Africa/FMCG; Margin: Normative ~21.5% but Q1/Q2 FY27 pressure expected due to crude oil; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex: New pet food plant in Nasik commissioned, Fab portfolio scaling.
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Fab portfolio ARR ~INR 500cr (GSV), INR 450cr (NSV), broken even in Q4.
segment / subsidiary detail: India Standalone: +10% sales, +18% EBITDA, 24.7% margin. Home Care +12% (Insecticides, Air Fresheners strong); Personal Care +3% (Soaps muted, Deodorants double-digit). International: Indonesia +3% sales (stabilizing); Africa/USA/ME +20% sales (media spend doubled); LatAm +26% sales (one-time cost impact).
growth verticals / optionality: Fab portfolio (Laundry Liquid) scaling to INR 500cr ARR, expanding nationally beyond South India; Pet Food category in product-market fit phase with new Nasik plant; Air Fresheners global export growth from India; Skin Cleansing portfolio shift (Body Wash, Face Wash via Muuchstac) compensating for soap maturity.
margins & cost dynamics: Blended RM inflation 7-9% (Crude @ $100-110/bbl, Palm Oil @ 4,500 MYR). Middle distillates (LAB/Kerosene) costs doubled. Pricing actions taken: Soaps +5%, Detergents +6-7%, Insecticides +4-5%. Q1/Q2 FY27 margin % pressure expected but absolute EBITDA protected via mix and pricing.
capex / expansion: Pet food manufacturing plant in Nasik commissioned; Ongoing investment in media spend for Africa FMCG franchise; Fab portfolio capacity scaling.
capital allocation: Investment ahead of curve in Africa media spend; M&A integration (Muuchstac, PAKS); Dividend policy not explicitly updated but cash flow unchanged by accounting reclassification.
risks & watch-items: Crude oil volatility impacting all categories simultaneously; El Nino weather patterns affecting Q1 Insecticide demand and soap volumes; Personal Care structural slowdown (soap to liquid shift); Competitive intensity in Indonesia despite stabilization.
management quality / tone: Confident in long-term compounding despite near-term margin headwinds; Transparent on accounting changes; Strategic pivot to Home Care and new categories emphasized; Cautious on Q1/Q2 margin % but optimistic on absolute profits.
non-obvious takeaways: The accounting reclassification of trade spend (netting vs. expensing) creates an optical margin expansion that masks the underlying cost pressure; The 'muted' soap volumes are partly due to lapping aggressive grammage reductions from prior quarters, not just demand weakness; Fab portfolio has already breached INR 500cr GSV run-rate, faster than anticipated, shifting from regional to national player.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crude oil inflation pressuring margins across FMCG peers | Godrej Consumer Products Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Diversified Home Care mix and pricing power in insecticides/detergents provide better hedging than soap-heavy peers; Fab portfolio growth offsets core slowdown. |
| Accounting opacity in trade spend reporting | Godrej Consumer Products Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Early adoption of ICAI guidance improves comparability long-term but creates short-term confusion for investors tracking historical margins. |

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Godrej Consumer Products Limited (GCPL) is an FMCG company within the over 125-year-old Godrej Industries Group, selling everyday consumer products across India & SAARC, Africa, Indonesia, Latin America and the United States.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GCPL manufactures and sells fast-moving consumer goods; management splits the portfolio into soaps (the business Ardeshir Godrej began with a vegetable-oil soap made for India) and a faster-growing non-soaps portfolio that includes household insecticides, hair care and air care. Its operations, including manufacturing sites, span India & SAARC, Africa, Indonesia, Latin America and the United States; the Integrated Annual Report is presented on a consolidated basis while the BRSR is standalone. Management characterises the company as strong on the classic FMCG playbook of big SKUs, general trade distribution and television-led media, and as still building capability in e-commerce, digital marketing and AI.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: India Standalone: +10% sales, +18% EBITDA, 24.7% margin. Home Care +12% (Insecticides, Air Fresheners strong); Personal Care +3% (Soaps muted, Deodorants double-digit). International: Indonesia +3% sales (stabilizing); Africa/USA/ME +20% sales (media spend doubled); LatAm +26% sales (one-time cost impact).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Mid-single-digit volume in Indonesia, double-digit in Africa/FMCG; Margin: Normative ~21.5% but Q1/Q2 FY27 pressure expected due to crude oil; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex: New pet food plant in Nasik commissioned, Fab portfolio scaling.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Fab portfolio (Laundry Liquid) scaling to INR 500cr ARR, expanding nationally beyond South India; Pet Food category in product-market fit phase with new Nasik plant; Air Fresheners global export growth from India; Skin Cleansing portfolio shift (Body Wash, Face Wash via Muuchstac) compensating for soap maturity.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Blended RM inflation 7-9% (Crude @ $100-110/bbl, Palm Oil @ 4,500 MYR). Middle distillates (LAB/Kerosene) costs doubled. Pricing actions taken: Soaps +5%, Detergents +6-7%, Insecticides +4-5%. Q1/Q2 FY27 margin % pressure expected but absolute EBITDA protected via mix and pricing.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Investment ahead of curve in Africa media spend; M&A integration (Muuchstac, PAKS); Dividend policy not explicitly updated but cash flow unchanged by accounting reclassification.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The report describes manufacturing footprint build-out rather than a rupee capex plan. Project Vindhya, GCPL's second greenfield project in India, was commissioned in March 2024 and is described as delivered in record time and designed to be digitally enabled, sustainably designed and inclusive by intent. A greenfield plant in Tamil Nadu is referenced, and the Chengalpattu manufacturing facility is described as a 27-acre plant built in just 13 months that has created over 1,000 job opportunities with 50% women on the shop floor. Other named sites appearing in the year's awards and operations commentary include the Kathua plant and the Nilgiri plant. On capability expansion: manufacturing enablement for LATAM markets was strengthened through completion of pending ammonia and no-ammonia hair-colour shades, while India continued to serve as a production hub for select international businesses; the hair colour category also progressed through miniaturisation initiatives, expansion of professional shade offerings and development of consumer-centric wet hair products. Nigeria's NAFDAC completed a GMP audit of the Aer pocket line successfully and export production started. R&D-led expansion included entry into new segments (antiperspirants with Bloq, plug-in electric fragrance with Aer Plug Electrical, women's fragrance EDP gift sets under Park Avenue/Kamasutra), a natural-ingredient Rat Repellent Spray, a Dimefluthrin-based Goodknight Aerosol and Liquid Vaporizer relaunch in Nigeria, higher-active Mat and Liquid Vaporizer formats in Indonesia, Renew Shampoo Hair Colour and Inecto Pop Shades and Bleach in South Africa, Hair Super Food variants in Nigeria, and multiple patents filed during the year. A value engineering initiative on the Good Knight device was commercialised, and a green solvent replaced a petroleum-derived solvent in Aerosol.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident in long-term compounding despite near-term margin headwinds; Transparent on accounting changes; Strategic pivot to Home Care and new categories emphasized; Cautious on Q1/Q2 margin % but optimistic on absolute profits.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Category leadership in incense: 'We are already the number one player and continue to gain market share rapidly', and the category is described as accretive to both revenue and profit growth - against a GCPL average net contribution of around 100 rupees, incense delivers roughly 80-85
- Long-cycle R&D depth: upcoming launches in hair and household insecticides in areas where the company says it has 'invested nearly a decade in research and development', with an innovation pipeline 'stronger than it has ever been'
- Distribution and mass-market execution: management self-assesses GCPL at the '80th or 90th percentile' on the classic FMCG playbook of big SKUs, general trade distribution and television-led media (and candidly at the ~50th percentile on e-commerce, digital marketing and AI)
- Structural health of the base business: penetration and market share in key categories have trended well, and India standalone non-soaps volume growth moved from low single digits in FY2022 to the teens in FY2026
- Sustainability standing: ranked number 1 on the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Sustainability Indices in FMCG this year
- Brand and group heritage: part of the Godrej Industries Group, crafting products since 1897, with 15% of the group owned by an independent philanthropic trust

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Crude oil volatility impacting all categories simultaneously; El Nino weather patterns affecting Q1 Insecticide demand and soap volumes; Personal Care structural slowdown (soap to liquid shift); Competitive intensity in Indonesia despite stabilization.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The accounting reclassification of trade spend (netting vs. expensing) creates an optical margin expansion that masks the underlying cost pressure; The 'muted' soap volumes are partly due to lapping aggressive grammage reductions from prior quarters, not just demand weakness; Fab portfolio has already breached INR 500cr GSV run-rate, faster than anticipated, shifting from regional to national player.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Aligning climate disclosure more closely with the TCFD framework in the current reporting cycle - covering climate governance, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, scenario analysis, metrics and targets - and preparing a first standalone TCFD report, alongside continued reporting through Integrated Annual Reports, CDP and DJSI
- Board-level climate oversight: a dedicated Board-level Sustainability Committee led by the Chair of the Board oversees sustainability performance, with the Managing Director and CEO approving climate strategies and reviewing sustainability KPIs quarterly, plus an …
